text: They probably read fewer books, but I'm not sure they read less overall. Teenagers spend hours reading messages, posts and articles online. The real difference is that this reading is fragmented — short pieces, constantly interrupted. What worries me is the ability to concentrate on a long text for an hour, because that's a skill you only develop by actually doing it.

tips.en: Fewer books, but not less overall draws an accurate line.
tips.kk: Fewer books, but not less overall — дәл айырмашылық.
tips.ru: Fewer books, but not less overall — точное различие.
tips.example: They probably read fewer books, but I'm not sure they read less overall

tips.ru: What worries me is … — ответ показывает главное.
tips.example: What worries me is the ability to concentrate

questions.question: Do young people read less than they used to?

text: Yes, but they'll probably look quite different. Fewer people need a library just to borrow books, but it's one of the last public places where you can sit for free, use a computer and study in peace. Many libraries already run language clubs and coding classes for children. If they keep adapting like that, I think they'll be more useful than ever.

tips.en: Yes, but they'll probably look quite different gives the answer a twist.
tips.kk: Yes, but they'll probably look quite different — бұрылысы бар жауап.

text: I think classics should be part of the curriculum, because they're a shared reference point for a whole culture. The problem is how they're taught. Forcing fifteen-year-olds to memorise long passages usually makes them hate the book. It would work better to mix classics with modern novels and let students discuss them freely, including saying honestly that they didn't enjoy something.

tips.en: The problem is how they're taught points to the method, not the content.

text: It depends on what you're looking for. A film can bring a story to life with music and images, and it's a good way to get into a long novel. But a book gives you access to characters' thoughts, which films usually lose. I'd say read the book first if you can, because once you've seen the film, it's hard to imagine the characters any other way.

text: Quality helps, of course, but it's rarely the whole story. Timing matters a lot — a book about a topic everyone is already discussing has a huge advantage. Recommendations are even more powerful nowadays, since one popular video on social media can sell thousands of copies overnight. So a bestseller often tells you more about what people are talking about than about the book itself.

tips.en: Rarely the whole story avoids an oversimplified answer.
